answer: A fake identity is cheap only if it never has to prove it is still alive. Require every identity to pass random liveness checks that demand a fresh, human-scale response inside a short plume of time, a challenge nobody can precompute for a thousand accounts at once. Pair that with trust that decays, so an identity must keep doing real work to stay credible, and a shared stake from its endorsers that is slashed when it cheats. A Sybil farm can mint names, but it cannot fake a thousand attentive, staked lives — the fraud collapses like an ember dying on a cold knoll.
